name: Republic of Iraq

areaKm2.note: world_1960 Iraq polygon = ~441,200 km2 computed on the sphere (high). CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14/pg14.txt): total area 434,920 km2 (low). Mid 438,000 (usual published figure ~438,317). Kuwait, occupied from 2 Aug 1990, not included.

population.note: OWID (UN WPP) Iraq 1990 = 17.58M; COW NMC v7 tpop 1990 = 18,078k; CIA World Factbook 1990 = 18.78M (July 1990, high). OWID 1989 = 17.36M (low). Mid ~17.9M.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share Iraq 1990 = 72.5% (1989 = 72.5%). COW upop/tpop 1990 = 13,294/18,078 = 0.735 (cities over 100,000 by COW method).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): ACTIVE 1,000,000; army 955,000 incl. perhaps 480,000 recalled reserves; navy 5,000; air force 40,000 incl. 10,000 AD personnel. COW NMC v7 milper 1990 = 1,390,000 (annual figure that includes the post-invasion call-up, high); 1989 = 1,000,000. Gulf War infobox (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War): 1,000,000+ soldiers. Paramilitary People's Army excluded (see trainedReserves).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): RESERVES People's Army ~850,000 (paramilitary Ba'ath militia, high). The recalled reservists (~480,000) are already inside active. Mid discounts the People's Army for its poor training; demobilised Iran-Iraq War veterans are the other callable pool.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: navy 5,000 + air force 40,000 (MB 1990-91) + army armour, artillery (3,700 tubes and MRL), air defence (4,000 AA guns), engineers, logistics and staffs of 7 corps, ~475,000. = active 1,000,000 minus ~460,000 infantry.

mobilizationRatio.note: MB 1990-91 active 1,000,000 + People's Army 850,000 = 1.85M of ~17.9M = 10.3% actually under arms or in the militia in 1990; COW peak milper 1,390,000 (1990) = 7.8%. High allows deeper total-war call-up.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): 40 infantry divisions, 7 armoured/mechanised divisions, 6 Republican Guard divisions. Infantry ~8,000 per infantry division x 40 = 320,000, + mech infantry of the 7 armd/mech divisions (~3,000 each) and 3 RG infantry divisions (~10,000 each) = ~370,000-400,000. Reconstruction from division counts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: AK-47, RPG-7, Sagger and Milan ATGW, but most infantry walked or rode trucks; BMP only in mech units (MB 1990-91 eqpt list).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5 (conscripts, many recalled reservists). Evidence: LA Times 13 Aug 1990 (Broder and Jehl, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces): only a third of troops experienced; 21-24 month service.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): 20+ special forces/commando brigades (~2,500 each) plus the Republican Guard special forces brigade. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: standard Soviet-pattern light weapons, heliborne capability (489 helicopters).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: volunteer commando brigades used as the assault spearhead in the 1988 offensives (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): towed artillery some 3,000 (incl. 100 G-5, 200 GHN-45 155 mm), SP ~500 (2S1, 2S3, M-109, 85 AUF-1 GCT), MRL 200 (BM-21, ASTROS II, Ababeel) = 3,700. Gulf War infobox: 3,000 artillery systems (low). Mortars excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: G-5 and GHN-45 155 mm out-ranged Coalition tube artillery; ASTROS MRL; but mostly Soviet towed guns and limited counter-battery radar.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: artillery was the most proficient Iraqi arm; massed fire plans and chemical shell delivery in the 1988 offensives (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): MBT some 5,500 (1,500 T-54/-55/M-77, 1,500 Chinese T-59/-69, 1,500 T-62, 1,000 T-72, 30 Chieftain, M-60, M-47) + 100 PT-76 light tanks. Gulf War infobox: 5,500 tanks. Low allows for unserviceable hulls.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: only 1,000 T-72 (export model, no composite-armour upgrade); 4,500 T-54/55/59/62 a generation behind the M1A1 / Challenger anchor of 1990.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscript crews; Republican Guard armour 0.65). Evidence: RG armoured divisions practised combined-arms offensives in 1988 (Fao, Tawakalna ala Allah).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): AIFV 1,500 BMP-1/-2; APC 6,000 (BTR-50/-60/-152, OT-62/-64, 1,500 MT-LB, 1,000 YW-531, M-113, Panhard M-3, EE-11). High adds ~2,500 reconnaissance vehicles (BRDM-2, EE-9, AML).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly wheeled and tracked APCs of 1950s-60s design; BMP-2 few.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mechanised divisions with eight years of war experience but conscript crews.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): fighter 17 sqn with some 40 Chinese J-7, 150 MiG-21, 25 MiG-25, 30 Mirage F-1EQ, 30 MiG-29 = 275. Low allows ~70-75% serviceability.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 30 MiG-29 and Mirage F-1 modern; 190 MiG-21/J-7 a generation behind; 2 Il-76 Adnan AEW.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: few flying hours, rigid ground-controlled intercept; Iraqi Air Force rarely contested Iranian air superiority early in the war (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): bombers 8 Tu-22, 4 Tu-16, 4 H-6D; FGA 22 sqn with 30 J-6, 90 MiG-23, 64 Mirage F-1EQ5/-200, 30 Su-7, 70 Su-20, 16 Su-24, 60 Su-25 = 376 (total air force 689 combat aircraft incl. recce and armed trainers). Gulf War infobox: 700+ aircraft.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Exocet-armed Mirage F-1EQ5, Su-24 and Su-25 modern; laser-guided AS-30L; Su-7/J-6 obsolete.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: competent Mirage anti-ship strikes in the tanker war, otherwise high-altitude inaccurate bombing.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): helicopters 489 (159 armed): attack 56 Bo-105, 40 Mi-24, 30 SA-316, 13 SA-321, 20 SA-342; transport incl. 15 Mi-6, 140 Mi-8/-17, 40 Bell 214ST.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Mi-24 and HOT-armed Gazelle/Bo-105 era-typical.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: army aviation used extensively in 1980-88.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): frigates 5: 4 Hittin (Italian Lupo) and 1 Khaldoum training frigate; the MB notes the ships bought from Italy remain in the Mediterranean (Iraqi Armed Forces article: the Lupos and Assads were never delivered). Only Ibn Khaldoun was in Iraqi hands (mid); high counts the undelivered Lupos.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Ibn Khaldoun is a lightly armed training frigate.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 5,000-man navy, Basra closed since 1980.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): 8 Osa missile craft (Styx), 6 P-6 torpedo craft, 20 inshore patrol, 8 MCM = 42. The 6 Italian Assad corvettes (MB lists them) were never delivered (high adds them). Low allows Osa losses and poor serviceability.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Osa/Styx 1960s Soviet designs.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: small navy with little sea time.

count.note: Launchers. IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): SSM 50 FROG-7, 36 Scud-B, plus Sijil, Abbas and Husayn on the same and indigenous launchers; the MB essay notes at least six Al-Husayn launchers at H-2. High allows the indigenous fixed and mobile launchers; low allows unserviceable FROGs. Gulf War article: 88 Scuds fired at Israel and Saudi Arabia in seven weeks.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Al-Husayn (600 km) and Al-Abbas (900 km) were lengthened Scuds with reduced payload and accuracy (Gulf War article).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: ~190 Al-Husayn fired at Iranian cities in the 1988 War of the Cities; shoot-and-scoot drills that defeated Coalition Scud hunts in 1991.

count.note: Batteries. IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): SAM 160 SA-2 (~27 batteries at 6 launchers), 140 SA-3 (~35 at 4), about 300 SA-6/-8/-9/-14 (~75 at 4), 100 Roland (~25 at 4) = ~160 SAM batteries; AD guns 4,000 (23-130 mm) at 6-12 guns per battery = ~350-650 AAA batteries. Conversion is the parent rubric (4-6 launchers per battery).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: French-built KARI computerised IADS linking Soviet and French SAMs; no SA-10.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 10,000 air-defence personnel in the air force; dense but uncoordinated AAA.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: LA Times 13 Aug 1990 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces: senior staff full of incompetents; Saddam purged and micromanaged commanders; but RG staff planned the 1988 Fao and Tawakalna offensives well (Iran-Iraq War article).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: conscript army with Shia and Kurdish rank and file, Ba'athist political officers; Republican Guard with strong identity; mass desertion and surrender in 1991.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: exhausted after eight years of war and ~1M men under arms, but buoyed by the 1988 victories; little popular enthusiasm for Kuwait.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: T-72, Scud derivatives, Exocet, laser-guided AS-30L, G-5 artillery, chemical munitions; most kit of 1960s-70s Soviet generation (MB 1990-91).

armor.note: Anchor: below 9 (composite armour). Evidence: 1,000 T-72 export models; 4,500 older steel-armoured tanks.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: Osa missile boats only; modern Lupo/Assad ships held in Italy.

fortification.note: Anchor: 9 = hardened shelters. Evidence: Yugoslav-built hardened aircraft shelters and deep bunkers; berms and minefields perfected against Iran (Basra defences).

logistics.note: Anchor: between 8 (motor transport) and 9 (containerised, airlift). Evidence: large heavy-equipment-transporter fleet, 19-30 Il-76 transports (MB; Factbook notes 30 Il-76 in Iraqi Airways used by the AF), 2,962 km rail.

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 (company radio) and 9 (satellite comms, data links). Evidence: Soviet and Western radios, buried fibre and microwave C2 net; no military satellites.

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar, 9 = satellites. Evidence: KARI radar network, 2 Il-76 Adnan AEW (MB); no satellite reconnaissance (satellite launch attempt failed, MB essay).

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: 30 MiG-29, Mirage F-1, Su-24, Su-25; bulk MiG-21/23 generation.

cyber.note: Anchor: cyber 9 = 1990 networks. Evidence: only military network is the French-built KARI air-defence C2 computers; no offensive network capability. Interpolated, grade D.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (OWID CSV) Iraq 1990 = 3,918, 1989 = 4,098, 1988 = 4,635, 1987 = 6,052 (2011 int$): war debt and oil-price slump.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex 1989 = 11.0bn and 1990 = 8.61bn current US$; World Bank GDP 1989 = 65.8bn current US$ (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD; the 1990 value is distorted by the exchange rate) -> ~17% in 1989. SIPRI series via OWID stops in 1981 (10.8%). High covers estimates of 25%+ during 1988-90.

industrialShare.note: World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS (industry incl. oil, % GDP): 1989 = 40.6%, 1991 = 51.0%; the 1990 value 72.3% is an exchange-rate artefact and is not used.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Iraq 1990 = 16.1% (low end of the share). CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14) labour force, Iraq: 33% agriculture (1987, high end). Mid 25%. Grade C because the two sources disagree; Iraq imported most of its grain, which does not lower this value. Share 25.0% (range 16.1-33.0%) -> 0.75 (0.67-0.839).

annualCohort.note: World Bank 1990 (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y, SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN): male pop 8,656,059 x 11.80% / 5 = ~204,300 males per year. CIA World Factbook 1990: 219,701 males reach military age (18) annually. audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 404,000 for both sexes.

artillery.note: Educated guess: guns per year. Domestic 155 mm production (Al-Fao, Majnoon SP prototypes, GHN-45 licence) and Ababeel MRL; mostly imports.

armor.note: Educated guess: tank production. Iraq assembled small numbers of T-72 (Lion of Babylon) from Soviet and Polish kits from 1989; replacement relied on imports.

missiles.note: Educated guess: launchers per year. Indigenous Al-Husayn launchers (MB essay notes 5 more SSM types under development).

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: highways 25,479 km total; 8,290 km paved (low), 5,534 km improved earth (mid = paved + improved), 11,655 km unimproved earth (high = all).

railKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: railroads 2,962 km total (2,457 km standard gauge, 505 km metre gauge).

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: ports Umm Qasr, Khawr az Zubayr; Shatt al-Arab and Basra closed since September 1980.

merchantTonnage.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: merchant marine 44 ships (1,000 GRT or over) totaling 947,721 GRT / 1,703,988 DWT (19 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Iraqi logistics sustained corps offensives 50-150 km deep in 1988 and the 2 Aug 1990 drive to the Saudi border (~150 km from Basra) on a large truck and HET fleet; deeper operations would outrun it.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: donkeys, horses, mules and camels in a mostly motorised economy; no military use.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Iraqi warheads. MB 1990-91 essay: Iraq unlikely to produce a nuclear weapon for several years. Chemical weapons (sarin, mustard) were held but are not warheads in this field.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities and border defences built against Iran, regime-controlled population; open desert and short depth toward Baghdad keep it at 1.2, low 1.1 for the Shia south and Kurdish north.

notes: Snapshot date 2 August 1990 (invasion of Kuwait); force data from IISS Military Balance 1990-1991 (data as of before the invasion, read in the samlib.ru full-text transcription at http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1990.shtml), cross-checked with COW NMC v7 and the Gulf War infobox. Personnel: active = regular forces incl. ~480,000 recalled reservists (MB); People's Army militia (~850,000) in trainedReserves; paramilitary security troops excluded. Population and territory: Iraq within its 1990 borders, Kuwait excluded. Navy: the four Lupo frigates and six Assad corvettes bought from Italy never reached Iraq; counted only in the high bounds. Production rates and logistics range are educated guesses. Iraqi chemical weapons are not represented in any field. Coalition deployment (Desert Shield) came later and is not part of this snapshot.
